Judgment:

1. This judgment shall decide the present appeal preferred by the appellants under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing order dated 22.04.2022 passed by Sh. Sh. Nagendra Shekhar Pati Tripathi, Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (Central) Delhi, whereby, the appellant have been imposed a penalty of Rs. One Lakh for violation of Section 26(2)
(ii) read with Section 3 (1)(zx) of the FSS Act, punishable under Section 51 of the FSS Act.

BRIEF FACTS:
2.

It is stated that on 07.10.2017, Sh. Bal Mukund, the Food Safety Officer alongwith other officials visited the premises i.e. M/s. Tomar Paneer Bhandar, 67, Ground Floor, Sanjay Market, Fatehpuri,
Delhi110 006 and purchased the sample of "Paneer" for analysis under the provisions of FSS Act/Rules/Regulations, for which credit note of Rs. 210/ dated 07.10.2017 was given.
The sealed sample packets along with a copy of memo in Form VI were sent to the Food Analyst, Delhi and also to the Designated Officer.

An opportunity was given to the appellant/Food Business Operator (FBO)
In Re vs Sh. Bal Mukund on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33921668/
1 for sending the fourth packet for analysis to NADL accredited Laboratory under Section 47(1)(c)(3)
and 2.4.5 of the rule.
The Food Analyst analyzed the sample and reported the sample to be substandard because moisture exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 60% vide its Report dated 12.10.2017.

Thereafter, the appellant was provided an opportunity to file an appeal u/s 46(4) of FSS Act within the stipulated period of 30 days, however, no appeal has been preferred by the appellant against the report of the Food Analyst.
During the course of hearing before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer, respondent/appellant herein submitted his written statement on 27.03.2018 stating therein that sample was taken on 07.10.2017,

on which date, the specification of moisture was according to previous act and amendment for 60% moisture came in the Gazette of India on 13.10.2017 and he was obeying the old directions of 70% moisture

. The FSO in his counter reply dated 14.01.2019 submitted that as per the directions dated 02.08.2017, FSSAI has revised standards for Milk and Milk Products and accordingly the Food Analyst has given his report dated 12.10.2017.

Thereafter,
Ld. Adjudicating Officer after going through the documents available on record found the appellant guilty for selling 'substandard food article' in violation of Section 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3 (1)(zx)
of the FSS Act and passed the impugned order dated 22.04.2022 thereby imposing a penalty of Rs.
One Lakh upon the appellant.

GROUNDS OF APPEAL:
3. The impugned order is assailed inter alia on the grounds that the Adjudicating Officer failed to see the true and correct scope and interpretation of Section 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3 (1)(zx) of the FSS Act visavis to the facts and circumstances of the present case; and that the Adjudicating Officer failed to appreciate that sample was taken on 07.10.2017, on which date, the specification of moisture was according to previous act and amendment for 60% moisture came in the Gazette of India on 13.10.2017 and he was obeying the old directions of 70% moisture; and that the Adjudicating Officer failed to appreciate the Section 49 of FSS Act while adjudging the quantum of penalty under this Chapter.
4. The respondent opted not to file any reply.
5. Heard Arguments.
6. None appeared for the appellant to advance arguments.
7. Sh. Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent addressed the arguments.

In all fairness, he has submitted that the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India (FSSAI), which is a regulatory body, has given directions on 02.08.2017 revising the standards for 'milk and milk products'.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The notice for operationalization of the amended regulations provided that parameters of milk moisture in Paneer shall be 60% (m/m).

Further, these directions were notified by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on 12.11.2017 and Food Business Operator was required to comply with the provisions of these regulations w.e.f. 01.07.2018 DECISION:
8.

entities.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the impugned order, the sample of Paneer taken from FBO i.e. appellan was reported to be substandard because the moisture exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 60%.
The same is based upon the Food Analyst Report dated 12.10.2017, as per which, moisture in the sample was found to be 63.12%.

In Re vs Sh. Bal Mukund on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33921668/
2 9.

The Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent has fairly admitted that when the sample from the appellant was lifted, directions issued by FSSAI dated 02.08.2017 were in operation but these directions were notified subsequently on 12.10.2017 and it was further prescribed in the notification that Food Business Operator shall comply with all the provisions of these regulations w.e.f. 01.07.2018.
10.
There is no doubt that notification which is dated 12.10.2017 came into operation on 01.07.2018 has to prevail over the directions given by the FSSAI dated 02.08.2017.
Thereby when the sample was lifted, the moisture contained in the sample was required to be up to 70%.
Strangely, while passing the impugned order, the Adjudicating Officer/ADM (Central) did not consider this aspect and imposed penalty of Rs.One Lakh upon the appellant.
Thereby the appeal is accepted and the impugned order dated 22.04.2022 is set aside.
11. The record of the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate alongwith copy of this Judgment be sent back.
File of appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
